business.name: Hook & Hoof New American Kitchen & Cocktail

evidence.observedFact: Hook & Hoof's current official site shows an active Downtown Willoughby restaurant, posts current kitchen hours, emphasizes customer experience, and sends standard table reservations to Resy.
The official contact page publishes current hours and says events/private parties are available on Sunday, Monday and Tuesday, with business contact handled by phone and a published email address.
Hook & Hoof's Resy listing describes the restaurant as reservation-based and showed no same-day online availability for the captured date, with the next availability shown for the following day.
The official website offers gift cards, showing an existing mechanism for driving future visits beyond the initial meal.

gaps.recommendedFix: Turn private-party and event guests into permissioned, tagged customer cohorts and trigger post-event return offers, referral prompts and measurable repeat-visit rewards.
Add structured event-inquiry capture and automated acknowledgement/follow-up around the existing phone/email private-party process while preserving staff control over final event booking.
Connect gift-card purchasers and redeemers to permissioned comeback sequences so gift-card activity can lead into measurable repeat visits instead of ending at redemption.

notes: The business is active and has both reservation and private-event demand surfaces. Same-day Resy unavailability is treated only as a booking-demand signal, not proof of lost bookings. The sales hypothesis is that event guests and gift-card customers can be retained and reactivated more systematically. No monetary loss is claimed.
